title: Setup alignment: set the part's X and Y axis directions by picking an edge or two points

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Proposed by the maintainer (filed by an agent), 2026-11-09: picking the "Y" axis by either an edge or two points, and then X as well, should be an option for aligning parts to the WCS.

**What:** a setup alignment mode that orients the part *within* the work plane, after (or independently of) laying it flat:
- **Y axis:** pick a straight edge, or two points; their direction becomes the setup's +Y (the user can flip the sense).
- **X axis:** the same, by an edge or two points. When both are picked, X is projected so X and Y stay perpendicular (Y wins, or the user picks which is primary; record the choice). When only one is picked, the other follows from the work-plane normal (right-handed: X = Y × Z).
- The axes are measured in the work plane (projected onto it), so a slightly tilted edge still gives a clean in-plane direction. A direction too close to the plane normal is refused by name.

**Relation to the other alignment work:**
- #330 (reopened): face to plane sets the *plane* (which way is down). This sets the *in-plane rotation* (which way X/Y point), so together they give a full part frame.
- #554 drops edge picking for *plane* alignment on the setup page, because an edge can't define a plane. Edges are valid here, because an edge does define a direction. The setup page should make clear which pick each mode takes (face for plane; edge or two points for an axis), so the face pick no longer fights edge snapping.
- #555: three points define a plane (and optionally a full frame from points 1 and 2). This mode can share its point-picking UI and apply path.
- The result applies to the part alignment (#326/#341) and leaves G54-G59 coming from the setup (one WCS per setup).

**Requirements:** one undoable command, validated at creation. Refused by name: a degenerate direction (zero length, two identical points), X and Y parallel, a direction along the plane normal, non-finite input. Undo restores the previous alignment.

**Done means:** tests for an edge at 30 degrees in the plane picked as Y rotating the part so that edge runs along +Y; two points picked as X doing the same for X; both picked giving perpendicular axes per the recorded rule; the degenerate and parallel cases refused by name; and undo/redo walking it.
